title: Route on probability mass, bounded by the ceiling and the ladder
description:
The routing rule, which the measurement changed. Two things it is NOT: not the argmax alone, and not the argmax with a confidence floor underneath it.

The dear model is chosen when the mass on the dear work types clears a threshold. With today's lineup that is P(design) + P(diagnosis) > 0.50, which routed 14 of a 49-tick sample to the dear model. The alternatives measured on the same sample: argmax alone sent 17 of 49, and argmax with a low-confidence fallback to the default sent 26 of 49 - more than half, which is the blunt version this rule exists to avoid.

Why mass rather than argmax plus a floor: every low-confidence case in the sample was construction-vs-design or mechanical-vs-diagnosis, which is to say the flash/full line itself, never a cheap-vs-cheap confusion. A tick split 0.45 design / 0.42 construction is not an unknown to be defaulted; it is a tick with 0.45 of design in it. The mass rule spends that number instead of discarding it, and it leaves one tunable where the other shape has two.

THE THRESHOLD IS PROVISIONAL AND MUST SAY SO WHEREVER IT IS WRITTEN. The sample could not validate the flash/full boundary, because every tick in it ran at its role's base model with no [tier_policy] declared, and its retries were wall-clock and hold failures rather than capability failures. 0.50 is a starting point from one measurement, not a finding.

What is NOT relaxed, and is the reason promotion is safe at all:
  - The CEILING still bounds everything. At the ceiling the next actor is a person, not a bigger model.
  - Failure still escalates underneath. The classification picks a START; a failed attempt still earns a rung. A mis-classified construction tick fails on flash and becomes full with nobody in the loop.
  - A tick's own prose still cannot promote it. The classifier may; an assertion in a description may not. That is the rule in internal/runconfig/tierpolicy.go being narrowed, not deleted - it existed to stop a DESCRIPTION buying an expensive model, and a classified work type is not prose.
  - No answer at all, or an unreachable classifier: fall back to [[tier_policy.start]] and the default. The feature degrades to today's behaviour rather than stopping a run.

Triage with `ticfac finding wne e1f1c9c35a65f9b55cf60383d06a750bc131e63f7485f37d02ddb4a107c2d609 --promote-as <tick> --by "<who>"`, `--discard --by "<who>"`, or — when it was repaired inside this epic — `--fixed-as <commit> --by "<who>"`; the tick closes and the finding rides to the close-out, which does not hand over while it is untriaged.
acceptance_criteria: A dispatch selects its model from the recorded distribution by mass over the dear work types, the threshold is configurable and documented as provisional, the ceiling still bounds the result, a failed attempt still earns a rung above whatever the classifier chose, an absent classification falls back to [[tier_policy.start]], and go test -short ./... passes
